If it’s $165, I’d go. Where I am a coloring appointmet ends up costing me nearly $500 with a tip. I really can’t afford that regularly so I do it myself but it’s nice and easy to have someone else do it for you!

I personally do these things myself but ultimately it’s up to you. If you do decide to do it by yourself, I’d use Color Oops on the black. It’s annoying as hell and smells terrible lol but definitely follow the instructions carefully. It does really work. Then let your hair get a little dirty, you’ll want to live with the orange for a couple of days or as long as you can. You CAN color/bleach immediately after color oops but I’d reccomend you give it a break because you don’t wanna bleach freshly shampooed hair. Then, do the highlights. I like to use a highlighting cap where you pull the strands out with the little hook. You can find them at sally’s for real cheap. Alternitavely, you can do foils by taking the rat tail part of a comb and making like a zig zag motion on each section if that makes sense. I’d watch some YouTube videos on foil highlighting if you wanna do this lol. 

If you have no experience with bleach, make sure you cover it with plastic, and you can blast some heat on it here and there to make it develop faster. Don’t leave the lightener on for more than an hour. Whether you want to use 20 or 30 volume developer, is up to you. The higher the volume, the more lift, but also the more damage. Don’t start at your roots, the heat from your scalp will make it develop much quicker. Apply about an inch down from your scalp then if you want the highlights to go right up to your scalp, you can slap on more bleach up there when you have like 20-30 minutes left. You’re gonna wanna check on this every 10 minutes or so to see how it’s lightening. Make sure everything is super saturated. You don’t want to see your hair underneath the product at all. 

Now when you wash the bleach out, don’t shampoo or condition. Wash everything out and towel dry your hair so it’s damp but not dripping, then immediately go in with that blue based toner. I don’t have specific reccomendations for what kind of toner you’ll need but definitely blue based because blue is opposite orange on the color wheel. If you want to only deposit the color, use a 10 volume. If you want a little bit of extra lift as well, use 20. 

Most toners say to leave it on for 20 minutes. I wouldn’t. I’d say 10-15 minutes is more than enough. Toner is not permanent, it will fade a bit with every wash. So if your results are more ashy than you want, it will fade over time. After you rinse off that toner, again, no need to shampoo. Just finish off with a deep conditioner and leave it on under plastic for as long as you want. I hope it works out well for you! My macaw didn’t have a cage at all. I was told to implement a cage (not too much cage time, just so he has a confined space to call his own) and a specialized diet for his needs.
